✦ The origin of this game

This format is inspired by the Zener cards, created in the 1930s by psychologist Karl Zener and used by J.B. Rhine at Duke University to study extrasensory perception. With 5 possible symbols, pure chance predicts one hit in every five attempts—modern science has found no reproducible evidence of real extrasensory perception in these experiments, but they remain an entertaining game for observing your own intuition.

This game is for recreation: it does not scientifically measure extrasensory abilities or predict decisions or events.
